methodology_note: FCF proxy is UNDERLYING PROFIT (management's preferred earnings measure), NOT operating cash flow. For ORA/DMF retirement village operators, reported operating cash flow is inflated by resident ORA receipts, which are capital/financing inflows the company must continuously redeploy into new units. The prior model used OCF ($548m) and produced an intrinsic value of $38.69 (263% upside) implying ~36x P/E - a multiple SUM has never sustained. This model uses Underlying Profit ($234.2m), discounts at cost of EQUITY (UP is already after finance costs, so net debt is NOT subtracted again), and caps terminal value at historical exit multiples.

historical_growth.note: Base case decelerates from 16% (below the 19% 5yr UP CAGR, reflecting a higher base and tougher NZ property market) toward a 7% Y5 rate, then 3% terminal.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: After correcting the duplicated FY2022 row (UP was actually 171.4, not 141.1), the 3yr UP CAGR is ~11% (FY23 +11%, FY24 +8.5%, FY25 +13.4%), well below the 18.96% 5yr anchor. The base-case Y1 growth of 16% sits above the corrected recent trend; consider re-running scenarios with a lower Y1 rate.

base.description: Underlying Profit grows ~16% decelerating to 7%, exit P/E capped at historical median 14.9x. Cost of equity 11% (NZ ~10% + small/mid-cap & leverage premium).

bull.description: Australia scales to ~300 units/yr, NZ property recovery lifts resale velocity & ORA pricing, rate cuts ease finance costs. Exit P/E to historical max 29x.

bear.description: Mid-cycle UP base (median FY18-25 x0.95), NZ property stagnation, Australia delays, RV Act mandatory buy-back reform raises capital intensity, debt pressure caps build rate. Exit P/E to historical min 12.7x. Cost of equity 12.5%.

sensitivity.matrix_note: Intrinsic value/share (NZD), base case growth [16,14,12,9,7%], Underlying Profit basis, exit P/E capped at 14.9x, across cost-of-equity (WACC) and terminal growth.

nta_cross_check.note: Stock trades at 36.7% discount to NTA of $13.753599999999999/share. NTA is an asset-based floor reflecting revalued investment property; the gap reflects the market's discount for $1.97bn net debt, RV Act regulatory risk, and NZ property uncertainty.

sanity_check.diagnosis: Prior model used Operating Cash Flow ($548.2m) as the FCF proxy. For an ORA/DMF operator, OCF is inflated by resident occupation-right receipts (capital inflows that must be redeployed into new units), overstating distributable cash ~2.3x. That produced IV $38.69 implying ~36x P/E vs 10yr median 14.9x.
sanity_check.fix_applied: Switched FCF proxy from OCF to Underlying Profit ($234.2m); discounted at cost of equity (no double net-debt subtraction since UP is post-finance-cost); added exit-P/E caps (bear 12.7x / base 14.9x / bull 29x) tied to the 10yr realised range.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Summerset at $8.70 trades on ~9x Underlying Profit and 0.63x NTA - below its 10-year minimum P/E (12.7x) and minimum P/NTA (0.89x). The thesis is income + steady demographic-driven growth at a depressed multiple, NOT a fair-value-revaluation multibagger. Base-case IV reflects a re-rate toward a normalised ~15x exit P/E on a compounding earnings base; downside is anchored by NTA. The prior OCF-based DCF (263% upside) was an artifact of treating capital inflows as free cash flow and is corrected here.
valuation_philosophy.key_change: FCF proxy: OperatingCashFlow -> UnderlyingProfit; added exit-multiple caps.
